label: echoed first token n right after <DEL>, short sequences (L=3, or L=4 with 2nd token n/u/w/v)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively (99% of mass) at the first copy step (recall_idx 1) where the input is the fed-back first original token and that token is n. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on any input token other than n. Strongly length-gated: L=3 holds ~66% of mass and fires ~95% of the time; L=4 holds ~33% but only fires reliably when the token being output (2nd original) is n, u, w or v (top activations are n n x / n u x); L>=5 essentially never. Magnitude is largest for L=3 with second token n or u; digits among the originals lower the rate. Weak residual activations at recall_idx 2 when n is the 2nd original token.

issues: Reported test scores reproduce exactly: precision 0.875, recall 0.684, F1 0.768, mass recall 0.907.

The structural claims hold on the dev profile. 100% of mass is in the copy phase and 0% in the original and delimiter phases. 100% of mass is on in_tok 'n'. recall_idx 1 holds 98.9% of mass and recall_idx 2 holds 1.0%. L=3 holds 66.5%, L=4 33.2% and L=5 0.3%.

Firing rates are as described. L=3 (recall_idx 1, in 'n') has precision about 0.95. L=4 with 2nd token n/u has precision 1.0. L=4 with w/v has precision only 0.55, so w and v are marginal members of the list. They are the main source of the test false positives (96 FPs, mostly 'n v ...' and 'n w ...' at L=4). L=5 has precision 0.002.
The magnitude claim is confirmed. For L=3, mass per active step is about 2.3x higher when the 2nd token is n or u.
The digit claim is only partly supported. At L=3, precision is 0.94 with digits vs 0.95 without, so essentially no effect. The effect only shows at L=4 (0.16 vs 0.22).

The misses (309 test steps, 9.3% of mass) are low-activation tails (0.01-0.07 of max) at L=4, recall_idx 1, input 'n', with other 2nd tokens. They form a graded weak tail of the same class rather than a separate systematic class.

Changing the L=4 token list gives no material gain on test. n/u only: F1 0.744 (precision 0.97). n/u/w: F1 0.777. n/u/w/v/2/s: F1 0.763. The original predicate is near the frontier, and the remaining recall gap is a graded weak tail.
